summary: Interleaved retry / ack ordering causing duplicate remote tool side-effects across Python streaming client + Go orchestrator
related_confluence_pages: Confluence: Runbook - Tool call idempotency semantics (internal)
description: Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate external tool/webhook invocations when using the Python streaming SDK (multiplexed session) in combination with their Go orchestrator. Duplicates happen intermittently after client retries and reconnects; appear to be correlated with concurrent short backoff retries and the orchestrator re-sending confirmation tokens. Impact: Duplicate downstream charges and duplicate emails sent to end users. Reported across multiple customer projects using dedicated capacity. Environment: Production (Dedicated, us-east cluster), Python SDK v2.4.1 streaming mode, Go orchestrator v1.9.2 using multiplexed channels over a single connection. Steps to reproduce and logs attached below.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a multiplexed Python streaming client with two logical streams over a single websocket connection, send a function-calling request that triggers an external webhook/tool.
2) Simultaneously, the Go orchestrator listens for the webhook callback and posts a confirmation back to the session using the SDK's per-action confirmation API.
3) Force a transient network blip (simulated with iptables DROP for 200ms) causing the Python client to reconnect and replay unacknowledged frames.
4) Observe that the external webhook receives two POSTs for the same logical funcall and the orchestrator reports a duplicate confirmation token mapping.
5) Reproduce more reliably by increasing concurrency and enabling small randomized client retry jitter in both SDKs.
logs: [go-orch] 2026-03-09T15:12:34Z INFO webhook_post: received callback id=cn-8b3 status=200
[python-stream] 2026-03-09T15:12:34Z WARN reconnecting: socket read timeout, replaying 2 frames
[gateway] 2026-03-09T15:12:34Z INFO client_replay: replayed frames count=2 mapping=[cn-8b3->nonce-A, cn-8c1->nonce-B]
comments: Customer (2026-03-10): We've seen 3 duplicate charges tonight correlated with a client reconnect spike. This occurs only when the client is multiplexing streams over one connection.
Support (2026-03-10): Thanks for the report — we've escalated to SRE and runtime. Can you confirm SDK versions and whether you're using per-action confirmation tokens or the session-wide ack?
Customer (2026-03-10): Python SDK v2.4.1 streaming, using per-action confirmation tokens. Go orchestrator confirms each tool run by exchanging the token back to the platform after the webhook fires.

SRE (2026-03-11): Initial hypothesis: replayed frames on reconnect are being remapped to the same confirmation token in the gateway, and the orchestrator sometimes re-posts the token when it doesn't see an ack. Investigating mapping table TTL and replay dedup window.

Eng (2026-03-11): Reproduced locally with an integration test that replays frames while concurrently confirming from another client. Observed nonce reuse from the Python client when the idempotency header is truncated by an edge proxy under high concurrency.
investigation_notes: 1) Reproduction: Integration harness that simulates multiplexing + transient disconnects reproduces duplicate POSTs within 20-40% of runs when client retry jitter is non-zero.

2) Root cause hypothesis: two separate but related failures combine: (A) python SDK short idempotency token generation (compact UUID) can collide or be truncated across proxies, and (B) gateway replay logic remaps replayed frame indices to existing session nonces without a strict at-most-once guard when confirmations arrive concurrently.

3) Observed evidence: gateway logs show mapping table entries were overwritten during concurrent replays; the orchestrator's confirmation request arrived during a small race window where the gateway had not yet marked the frame as acked.
4) Secondary contributing factor: Go orchestrator will re-send confirmation on timeout; combined with frame replay this causes duplicate external webhook side effects.
5) Affected surface: all multiplexed streaming use with per-action confirmation tokens; more likely with edge proxies that shorten headers or use h2 header coalescing.
mitigation_and_workarounds: Short-term workaround (customer): Disable multiplexing and use one connection per logical stream until we patch the gateway. This dramatically reduces replay races.

Alternate workaround: Switch to session-scoped at-least-once semantics with explicit server-side dedupe using confirmation token finality — store confirmation token on your webhook side and ignore duplicates.
Edge workaround: Increase client idempotency token entropy (upgrade SDK or set custom idempotency_key per funcall) to avoid truncation collisions through proxies.
Support guidance: If on Dedicated, consider temporarily routing traffic through a direct path that avoids the problematic edge proxy.
planned_fixes: 1) Runtime/Gateway: Add strict replay dedup window keyed by full idempotency token + session and mark frames acked atomically to avoid remap races (ENG-3245).
2) SDKs: Ship Python SDK patch to emit longer idempotency tokens by default and to retry with exponential backoff and jitter coordination exposed (PY-SDK-2.4.2).
3) Go orchestrator best-practice doc: Add guidance on idempotency finality and confirm-once semantics and sample dedupe storage pattern.
4) Monitoring: Add a metric that tracks funcall duplicate rate by session and by edge-proxy to alert on regressions.
Related follow-up ticket: INT-999210 gateway replay atomicity postmortem and patch rollout.
resolution: Workaround validated: customer disabled multiplexing and duplicate invocations stopped. Eng implemented a Python SDK patch to increase default idempotency token length and server-side gateway patch to atomically mark frames acked. A full rollout to Dedicated clusters scheduled 2026-03-20. Customer confirmed temporary mitigation and will schedule migration to patched SDK/infra.
